summary: Milo Cleveland Beach is an art historian and Indologist. Educated at Harvard College and Harvard University, he taught at Williams College (1969–1984) and directed the National Museum of Asian Art and Freer Gallery of Art (~1988–2001).

Miloslav Krása was an Indologist and historian who studied at Charles University under Vincenc Pořízka (1943–1947) and at the University of Allahabad (1947–1948). He later served as a teacher at Charles University from 1954 to 1997.

Miloš Borecký was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological scholar. He earned his Ph.D. at Charles University under Vincenc Lesný and Jan Rypka, and later worked at the National Library of the Czech Republic (~1936–1954).

Milton Singer worked in Indology and religious studies. After earning his B.A. from the University of Texas at Austin and his Ph.D. under Rudolf Carnap at the University of Chicago, he served there as Professor of Anthropology (1954–1979).

Min Lin specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. A postgraduate student at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005–2006), Lin held a post as Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2026.
Min Ling Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin pursued studies under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Min Thu Wun was a linguist who studied under Pe Maung Tin at the University of Rangoon (~1927–1935) and continued his education at the University of Oxford (~1936–1939).
Minakshi Banerjee is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Debarchana Sarkar and held a James Prinsep Research Fellowship at The Asiatic Society in 2026.
Ming Chen is a scholar of Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who held a professorship at Peking University, attested in 2001 and 2013.

Ming Mei is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.Phil. at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan, and also studied at SOAS University of London under Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, and Shane McCausland.

Ming-Wood Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He earned a Ph.D. at UCLA under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en and Robert C. Epp before serving as a professor at the University of Hong Kong (~1980–2012).

Mingqian Xu is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Xu earned an MA at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and a PhD at National Chengchi University, later working as a Project Research Assistant at Dharma Drum (2013–2015).
Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Huifeng Shi (attested 2013).

Mini Verma is an Indology scholar who taught at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (2006–2007), Sai Group of Institutions (2007–2013), Institute of Management Studies, Noida (2013), and Jagannath Institute of Management Sciences, Noida (2022).

Minori Nishimura is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Taisho University under Shunkyo Katsumata and Seiren Matsunami. Nishimura held posts at Taisho University and Sanko Cultural Institute.

Minoru Hara was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo and president of ICPBS (1996–2006).

Minoru Inaba is a historian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (1980–1986). Inaba served as an assistant professor at Kyoto University (1992–2002) and became a professor at Doshisha University in 2008.

Minoru Kiyota was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and others. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1966 to 1999.

Minton Warren was a linguist who studied at Tufts, Yale under William Dwight Whitney, and Strasbourg. He served as Associate Professor of Latin at Johns Hopkins (1879–1899) and became a Latin professor at Harvard University in 1899.
Minyak Kunzang Sonam pursued studies under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
